subject: Acme - Post-call recap & integration follow-ups (SDK, auth, routing, prompts)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + Demo — follow-up & architecture questions

Hi Alex / Sara —

Great to chat earlier — thanks for walking us through Acme's search-driven product roadmap. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:  

Summary of the discovery call:
- Primary use case: in-app knowledge assistant that uses product docs + support transcripts to answer user queries.
- Non-negotiables: PII redaction, strict data residency for EU customers, and predictable 95th percentile latency under 200ms for single-turn queries.
- Important features: embeddings for semantic search + reranker layer, tool calling for database lookups, and structured output for UI rendering.

Integration follow-ups we discussed (please confirm):
1) SDK setup & auth: you asked about client SDKs and whether we support API keys and OAuth/KMS integrations for Private deployments.
2) Routing & model variants: how to route to smaller quantized models vs. larger models for quality-critical routes.
3) Structured output / tool calling: JSON-schema validation and how our tool-calling interface plays with prompts.
4) Embeddings + reranker: recommended workflow and hit/refresh cadence for embedding index updates.
5) Prompt governance: prompt versioning, guardrails against prompt injection, and red-teaming cadence.

Attachments: attaching our SDK quickstart and a short checklist for prompt governance.

Next steps I propose:
- Follow-up technical workshop w/ your architects + our Solutions engineer (Priyom) — 60–90 min deep-dive (routing, auth, structured output).
- Security alignment with Neha (our security lead) to cover data residency & audit logs.
- Share current architecture diagram from Acme so we can map routing and caching ops.

Can you confirm availability for a tech workshop next week (Feb 17–19)? Also please attach your current architecture diagram (if possible) so Priyom can pre-read.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap. Confirming availability on Feb 18 for a workshop (2–3pm PST).

Quick answers to your numbered items and what we’ll bring to the workshop:
1) SDK & Auth: We prefer using short-lived OAuth tokens via our identity provider (Okta) to avoid long-lived keys. For Private deployment, we will need KMS-backed key management.
2) Routing: We will want a fallback policy: default to a medium-sized model for standard queries, escalate to high-capacity model for long-form generation and escalation flows.
3) Structured output: We will rely on JSON fragments returned by the model to populate UI components — schema validation is a hard requirement.
4) Embeddings: We currently batch-update embeddings nightly; concerned about cold-start for new docs — curious about Redis/KV cache strategies you mentioned.
5) Prompt governance: We have a product-owned prompt repo and are starting to version prompts in Git, but we need guidance for prompt injection hardening and an internal red-team process.

Attached: acme_architecture_v1.pdf (high-level diagram). We’ll bring our data retention & PII handling policy doc to the workshop.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Subject: RE: Intro + Demo — follow-up & integration questions (workshop plan)

Hey team — thanks Marissa / Alex. I put together the tech plan below for the workshop and included concrete examples you can pre-read.

Workshop plan (90 min) — goals: verify integration architecture, prototype structured output flow, and align on prompt governance + security:  
- 0–10m: Introductions & goals
- 10–30m: Auth & SDKs demo (short-lived OAuth flow; Private KMS example) — show code snippet for obtaining scoped tokens
- 30–55m: Routing & model policies — show a policy example and fallback behavior (quantized variant)
- 55–75m: Structured output + tool-calling demo — example JSON schema enforced server-side and tool-calling to a secure DB lookup
- 75–90m: Prompt governance + red-team plan — versioning, test harnesses, injection mitigations, next steps

Technical notes / pre-reads (short):
1) SDK + auth snippet:
   // pseudocode
   token = oauth.exchange(auth_code)
   client = RedwoodClient(auth=token)
   resp = client.generate(model="rwd-medium-v1", prompt=prompt)

2) Routing policy example (pseudo YAML):
   routes:
     - name: default
       match: user_query.length < 200
       model: rwd-medium-v1
     - name: high-quality
       match: intent == "compose_long_form"
       model: rwd-large-v1
     - fallback: quantized-small-v1

3) Structured output & validation: we recommend returning a strict JSON object and validating server-side. Example schema (simple):
   {"type":"object","properties":{"action":{"type":"string"},"payload":{"type":"object"}},"required":["action"]}

4) Prompt versioning & governance: recommended minimum: prompt_id (uuid), semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR), change log, automated unit tests (prompt -> golden outputs), and CI gating for prompts that touch PII-sensitive templates.

5) Prompt injection mitigations (recommended layers):
- Input sanitization (strip suspicious system tokens/metadata)
- System prompt anchoring: prepend immutable system policy that disallows certain instructions
- Response validators: schema checks + classifier-based policy checks to catch anomalous outputs
- Runtime guardrails: if a prompt triggers policy flags, route to safe-mode model or human review

6) Red-teaming cadence: start with internal red-team once/month for high-risk prompts, quarterly external pen-tests for production routes, and a prompt-regression test in CI for every prompt change.

Action items before the workshop:
- Alex: confirm sample queries / escalation flows to test (2–3 examples).
- Acme infra: provide any rate/latency SLAs you need enforced.
- Marissa: set up calendar invite for Feb 18 2pm PST (90 min).

Happy to expand any section in advance — I can also prepare a short demo that shows JSON-schema enforced outputs and an example tool call to a mock DB (no PII in demo).

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
